sources.entry: This is a list of Free Software network services and web applications which can be hosted on your own server(s). Non-Free software is listed on the Non-Free page.

summary.name: Network service
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article defining a network service as an application at the network layer and above that provides data storage, communication or other capabilities, usually via client–server or peer-to-peer protocols.
use_cases: learning which ports common services use
choosing between TCP and UDP for an application
understanding DNS and DHCP roles on a network
summary.what_it_does: The page explains that a network service is an application running at the network layer and above, typically built on client-server or peer-to-peer architectures. It describes examples such as DNS, DHCP, authentication servers, email, printing and distributed file systems. It covers the application layer of the Internet protocol suite and notes that many IP services use well-known port numbers, for example port 80 for web servers and port 25 for email relay. It also contrasts TCP, used for reliable in-order delivery such as file transfer, with UDP, used for real-time services such as audio conferencing.
notable: Explains client-server and peer-to-peer service models
Lists well-known port examples such as HTTP port 80 and SMTP port 25
Compares TCP and UDP suitability for different services
caveats: Encyclopedia entry, not a tool; it does not describe any software product
UDP lacks built-in congestion avoidance, so protocols using it must be carefully designed
